description: Committee recommends one-way protected bike lanes for Victoria Avenue.
Project would remove on-street parking, add sidewalks.
Construction costs $3.64 million; snow removal increases annually.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 1 against
Councillor Pearce questioned the 'if we build it, they will come' mentality for bike lane usage.
Taxpayers would fund an annual snow removal increase of $187,000.
No data exists on winter bike traffic for this specific Victoria Avenue segment.
Public engagement showed mixed support
Councillor Pearce opposed due to lack of usage data and high snow removal costs.
Staff will provide information on how other cities fund active transportation projects.

segments.title: Staff Presentation: Project Background and Rationale
description: City's growth plan (2016) outlined eight key directions.
Plan aims for robust transportation network, all modes.
Traffic modeling shows congestion without mode shift.
Cycling mode share is not increasing, safe space needed.

chips.text: Current snow removal costs $38,000 per year
Growth plan supports sustainable development

segments.title: Staff Presentation: Existing Conditions and Design Options
description: Victoria Avenue identified as a cycling corridor.
Existing raised cycle track from bridge to 8th Street.
Project area: Taylor Street to Ruth Street.
Existing conditions include low parking, missing sidewalks.

chips.text: Option 1 estimated cost $3.6 million
Mature trees and private driveways impacted by in-boulevard options

segments.title: Staff Presentation: Recommended Design and Implications
description: One-way protected bike lane is the recommended option.
Design includes intersection improvements and sidewalk infill.
On-street parking demand is very low.
Winter maintenance costs will significantly increase.

chips.text: Estimated construction cost for Option 1 is $3.64 million
Removal of only three trees required for sidewalk installation

segments.title: Staff Presentation: Public Engagement Results
description: Two rounds of public engagement were completed.
Majority supported walking and cycling improvements.
Concerns raised about parking and tree removal.
Adjacent residents more likely to oppose cycling infrastructure.

chips.text: Majority of people supported improvements for walking and cycling

segments.title: Staff Presentation: Next Steps
description: Detailed design and cost refinement in future budget.
Project remains on transportation master plan list.
Administration will seek alternate funding sources.
Construction proceeds only once funding is secured.

chips.text: Project will remain on transportation master plan list

segments.title: Councillor McDonald's Questions
description: Questions traffic volumes for neighborhood bikeways.
Asks about impact of new builds on traffic counts.
Inquires about cyclist confusion with different infrastructure.
Asks if surveys should ask about infrastructure usage.

chips.text: Surveys did not specifically ask if people would use infrastructure
Does it get very confusing for people and cycle, like not only cyclists, but also, um, drivers.

segments.title: Councillor Ford's Questions
description: Asks for data on active transportation and safety improvements.
Inquires about the project's motivation (safety, growth, AT).
Questions the significant increase in snow removal costs.
Asks about changing snow removal priority levels.

chips.text: No specific data on how bike lanes improve active transportation
Snow removal cost increase of $187,000 annually

segments.title: Councillor Pears' Questions
description: Questions the low current bike traffic numbers.
Asks about the type of physical barriers to be installed.
Inquires about winter bike traffic data for the route.
Asks if snow clearing would be necessary without winter data.

chips.text: What physical barriers are actually going to be installed?

segments.title: Mayor Block's Questions
description: Asks about consistent infrastructure experience from downtown to Ruth.
Inquires about consideration for houses backing into lanes.
Discusses strategy of shelf-ready projects for funding.
Asks about an update on the city's growth plan.

chips.text: Shelf-ready projects align with funding opportunities
Cyclists prefer long stretches of same type of infrastructure

segments.title: Chair's Follow-up Questions and Clarifications
description: Follows up on new builds' impact on traffic counts.
Clarifies committee's authority regarding the report.
Asks about budget inclusion for detailed design.
Inquires about snow removal priorities for bike lanes.

chips.text: Committee cannot kill the matter, needs direction
Bike lanes downtown have been removed

segments.title: Committee Debate and Vote
description: Mayor Block supports, citing good planning and growth strategy.
Councillor Pears opposes, questioning justification and cost.
Chair supports, despite snow removal cost concerns.
The recommendation to approve the report carries.

chips.text: Recommendation to approve the report carries
Councillor Pears opposed the recommendation
Mayor Block states 'We need to stay the course' on planning
Councillor Pears states 'I don't believe it's wise to approve it at this point'

description: Committee recommends new limited residential parking zone in Nutana East.
New zone responds to two resident petitions.
The zone costs $4,700 from existing budget.
City Solicitor to amend parking bylaw.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Staff confirmed permit fee increases could achieve cost recovery for parking zones.
Residents in three Nutana East blocks will be affected by new parking rules.
A broader review of the residential parking program will be completed by fall 2026.
